best_for: Java and Kotlin developers who want JetBrains' IDE for free at work or at home, and who may pay for Ultimate once they need Spring tooling, the profiler or AI help.

points.title: One download, free core
points.text: Since 2025.3 there is a single IntelliJ IDEA installer. Core Java and Kotlin work is free for commercial and personal projects and needs no activation.

points.title: Former Ultimate pieces now free
points.text: The free tier now includes database connections, full SQL support, a Spring Boot project wizard, basic Spring and Jakarta EE highlighting, and LSP support.

points.title: What Ultimate still holds
points.text: Full Spring tooling, the IntelliJ Profiler, the HTTP Client and AI assistance need an Ultimate subscription. Every install starts a 30-day Ultimate trial, which needs a connection to activate.

points.title: Lapsing is not a lockout
points.text: If the subscription ends, the IDE keeps working with the free features. A fallback license also keeps the major version that was current when your last unbroken subscription year began, without updates.

points.title: Hardware it expects
points.text: JetBrains lists 8 GB of RAM, a 4-core x86_64 or Arm64 CPU and 10 GB of disk, on Windows 10 or 11, macOS 26 or 27, or recent Ubuntu, Fedora and Debian with GNOME or KDE. A Java runtime is bundled, but you still need a JDK to build Java code.

points.title: Linux Flatpak is not JetBrains'
points.text: The Flatpak here comes from Flathub, which does not mark it as verified by JetBrains. JetBrains itself suggests the Toolbox App or its .tar.gz archive.

points.title: Installs and history
points.text: The Windows installer comes for x64 and Arm64 and can install per user or for all users. The Windows listing keeps 17 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
